name: rmdir
description: Removes a directory only if it is empty. This is a safety net: if the directory still contains something, rmdir refuses and prints an error. To delete a directory and its contents, you need rm -r.

options.description: Also removes parents that become empty: rmdir -p a/b/c removes c, then b, then a.
Prints a message for each directory removed.
Prints no error for non-empty directories (they are simply left in place).

examples.explanation: Removes the directory if it is empty.
If the directory is not empty, rmdir refuses.
examples.output: rmdir: failed to remove 'project': Directory not empty

examples.explanation: Removes c, then b, then a, as long as they are empty.
